coverage_gaps: ONLY 6 OF THE 8 PROMISED SUBSYSTEM ANALYSES ARE PRESENT in the condensed output. The two missing ones map almost exactly onto the largest orphaned areas below (BLE wire protocol/crypto, and the build-time safety-invariant tooling). Do not treat this set as complete PRD input.

THE ENTIRE BLE WIRE-PROTOCOL LAYER, ~10,400 LOC, UNCLAIMED. Verified: plugins/shipped/tandem/src/main = 4,527 LOC; plugins/shipped/medtronic/src/main = 5,838 LOC. Only 'shipped reference drivers (what a real driver looks like)' was claimed, and only at the level of driver *shape*. Nothing claims: ble/protocol/{TandemProtocol, Packetize, PacketAssembler, Crc16}; ble/connection/{BleConnectionManager, BleScanner, TandemBleDriver}; ble/auth/{TandemAuthenticator, JpakeAuthenticator, HmacHelper, AuthState}; ble/crypto/{EcJpake, Hkdf, HmacSha256Util}; ble/messages/StatusResponseParser (973 lines of byte-level opcode parsing); or the whole Medtronic stack (MedtronicCodec, PduFramer, SakeHandshakeDriver, MedtronicSakeSession, SerialWorker, MedtronicReadGateway, CgmReader, IddStatusReader, IddFeatures, HistoryReader, BatteryReader, DeviceInfoReader, MedtronicHistoryParser, MedtronicGattLink, AndroidMedtronicPeripheral). This is the layer where a bug becomes a wrong glucose or insulin number, and it is the largest unscoped item in the port.

CRYPTO WITH NO APPLE-PLATFORM EQUIVALENT, unclaimed by all six analyses. (a) Tandem EC-JPAKE is built on BouncyCastle: ECNamedCurveTable, raw ECPoint arithmetic on P-256, a custom ZKP encoding, fixed-length 32-byte scalar encoding, plus HKDF and HMAC-SHA256. CryptoKit exposes no raw EC point arithmetic and no J-PAKE; this needs swift-crypto/_CryptoExtras/BoringSSL or hand-rolled BigInt+P-256. (b) Medtronic depends on org.openminimed:javasake 0.2.0 (Maven Central, JVM-only) for the 6-stage SAKE handshake and the SeqCrypt session cipher, PLUS BouncyCastle for AES-CMAC, which build.gradle.kts notes 'the JDK/Android JCE does not provide' -- and CryptoKit does not provide it either. Neither library exists on Apple platforms. Both must be reimplemented in Swift and byte-validated. This alone is likely the longest-pole engineering task in the project.

THE THIRD CROSS-REPO SAFETY CONSTANT IS MISSING FROM EVERY ANALYSIS. docs/contract/safety-constants.md names exactly three drift-guarded constants: 18.0156, the 20..500 bound, and TANDEM_EPOCH_OFFSET = 1199145600 (2008-01-01 UTC), which lives in StatusResponseParser.kt:39. All six analyses covered the first two and none mentioned the third. Pump time is a uint32 seconds-since-2008 value; a wrong offset shifts every timestamp by decades and silently destroys the entire freshness/staleness/coverage-honesty architecture the alerting and wear subsystems rest on.

egvStatusId GATING IS UNCLAIMED. StatusResponseParser.kt:202 -- 'if (egvStatus !in 1..3) return null' -- accepts VALID/LOW/HIGH and rejects INVALID(0) and UNAVAILABLE(4+). This is the sensor's own claim that the value is usable, and it is entirely independent of the 20..500 bound that every analysis enumerated. A Swift port that drops it renders warmup and error sentinel values as real glucose. It belongs in the same tier as the 20..500 sites.

PUMP-PROTOCOL SEMANTICS NOBODY LISTED, all in StatusResponseParser: the iobType byte selecting between mudaliarIOB (Control-IQ off) and swan6hrIOB (Control-IQ on) -- showing the wrong one is dosing-relevant misinformation; per-field milliunit scaling that is NOT uniform (bolus/basal/IoB are milliunits divided by 1000, but reservoir is WHOLE units at 2 bytes -- an easy and dangerous port error); the bolusTypeBitmask 0x0A correction test; bolusSourceId (0=GUI, 1=AUTO_PILOT, 2=AUTO_POP_UP) and bolusStatusId (0/2/3/4) vocabularies; the V1 17-byte vs V2 20-byte LastBolusStatusResponse layout switch keyed on a 0x01 prefix byte (firmware 7.7+); the cgmTrendIconId 1..7 to CgmTrend mapping (the single most-read element in the app is sourced here, from opcode 57, not from the CGM response); and basalStatusIconId / apControlStateIconId, which are the source of the chart's activity-mode bands and the Sleep/Exercise PumpActivityMode enum.

presentation/pairing/ IS UNCLAIMED (963 LOC: PairingScreen.kt 775, PairingViewModel.kt 188). Settings claimed the pump *card* (pair/re-pair/unpair buttons) and the plugin subsystem claimed PairingProfile/PairingFault as types, but the actual pairing experience -- scan list, device selection, pairing-code entry, the advertise-and-wait UI with its own isAdvertising state and advertiseJob, and credential persistence on success -- is owned by nobody. It is also the screen most affected by the CBPeripheral-UUID-not-MAC change and by the Medtronic peripheral-role redesign.

THE BUILD-TIME SAFETY-INVARIANT MACHINERY IS UNCLAIMED AS A CAPABILITY. SafetyConstantDriftGuardTest, SafetyConstantWearGuardTest, ContractSmokeTest, the .coderabbit.yaml Medical-Safety path rules, attribution-check.yml, secrets-plumbing-check.yml, the SPDX header policy, and the generateDependencyAttribution Gradle task that fails the build when a resolved dependency has no license entry. Every analysis says 'port all N sites of the 20..500 bound'; none scopes the mechanism that KEEPS the ~14 enumerated sites equal. iOS multiplies the surfaces (app + watch app + iOS widget + watch widget, two separate App Groups, no shared defaults across the phone/Watch boundary), so this needs to be a first-class PRD story, not an afterthought. docs/adr/0003 already records the consolidation follow-up.

tools/medtronic-ble-spike/ IS UNCLAIMED. It is an offline, re-runnable de-risk harness that validates the SAKE handshake byte-for-byte against a captured 780G pairing trace, plus android-peripheral-probe with a peripheral-mode support matrix. The plugin analysis correctly calls advertise-and-wait the highest-variance unknown and says 'prototype against real hardware first' -- but does not notice that a hardware-free, trace-driven acceptance harness already exists. Given Core Bluetooth is absent from the Simulator, porting this harness to Swift is arguably the single highest-leverage early task: it makes the Swift SAKE reimplementation verifiable with no pump.

LIVE PUMP-STATUS METRICS ARE STAMPED WITH RECEIVE TIME, NOT DEVICE TIME. parseIoBResponse, parseBasalStatusResponse, parseInsulinStatusResponse and parseBatteryV1/V2Response all set timestamp = Instant.now(); only parseCgmEgvResponse carries a device timestamp (pumpTimeSec + epoch). So the PUMP freshness tier (15 min STALE / 60 min TOO_STALE) measures POLL RECENCY, not data age, by construction. No analysis states this, and it interacts directly with every iOS background-cadence redesign -- the pump tier means something materially different when polls are BLE-event-driven instead of every 15 s.

STORE OWNERSHIP GAPS: GlucoseRangeStore (display target range) is named only in a 'do not merge these' warning and is claimed as a capability by nobody. Same for PumpProfileStore (maxBolusUnits 0f..25f validation) and the SafetyLimitsStore clamp-on-write/clamp-on-read reconciliation as an owned surface rather than as a constant.

NON-GAPS WORTH RECORDING SO THEY ARE NOT REDISCOVERED (verified absent from the Android repo): no Health Connect / androidx.health integration; no AppWidgetProvider, TileService, ShortcutManager, or deep links (MainActivity is exported but processes no intent data, per an explicit manifest comment); no data export or ACTION_SEND share; no localization at all (single values/ resource set, no values-xx, strings.xml is 9 lines -- essentially all copy is inline in Kotlin); allowBackup=false. Consequence for the PRD: the iOS widgets, Lock Screen widgets, Smart Stack and complications proposed across five analyses are ADDITIVE SCOPE, not parity restoration. They are how the lost Wear watch face and the lost foreground-service notification are approximated -- that framing should be explicit, because it is a large amount of net-new work under a 'parity' banner.
contradictions: READ-ONLY-BY-CONSTRUCTION vs CalibrationTarget.calibrate(). The data-layer analysis states it absolutely: 'PumpDriver intentionally exposes NO insulin-delivery, pump-setting or control methods; every method is a read-only status query.' The plugin analysis contradicts this: CalibrationTarget.calibrate(bgValueMgDl, timestamp) is a device WRITE that it reclassifies as 'session/lifecycle, not therapy', and PluginRegistry.kt:87-88,436 maintains a live activeCalibrationTarget slot. I verified no shipped driver implements CalibrationTarget -- it is an UNUSED WRITE SURFACE in the SDK. The mandate says 'monitoring-only, read-only, never issues therapeutic writes'. Porting CalibrationTarget into the Swift DriverAPI carries a write capability into a binary whose App Review notes will claim read-only. Compounding it, the plugin analysis notes capability enforcement at the registry boundary is 'PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED'. Recommended verdict: omit CalibrationTarget from the iOS DriverAPI entirely.

FRESHNESS MUST USE THE SENSOR'S OWN TIMESTAMP -- except pump metrics have none. Alerting states the rule absolutely ('Age is computed against the CGM's OWN sensor timestamp, never poll wall-clock'); the plugin/Nightscout analysis restates it ('STALENESS IS TIMESTAMP-BASED AND SOURCE-AGNOSTIC'). But StatusResponseParser stamps IoB/basal/reservoir/battery with Instant.now(). The PUMP tier therefore measures poll recency by construction, which is a different quantity from the CGM tier. Nobody flagged it, and it is exactly the axis iOS changes most.

NIGHTSCOUT VALIDATES AGAINST ABSOLUTE BOUNDS; TANDEM BLE VALIDATES AGAINST THE USER'S SafetyLimits. The plugin analysis states this asymmetry is deliberate. Verified in code: parseCgmEgvResponse rejects on limits.minGlucoseMgDl/maxGlucoseMgDl (backend-syncable, user-scoped) while CgmReading's constructor requires absolute 20..500. Consequence nobody drew: a backend that narrows SafetyLimits silently drops BLE readings the same app would accept from Nightscout. The identical glucose value can be present or absent depending on source, which changes TIR, GMI, CV, the chart, and the alert floor's input set. Neither the core-display nor the alerting analysis accounts for it.

ALERT-FLOOR GATE 1 ('server alerting degraded') -- opposite risk verdicts on the same mechanism. Alerting recommends keeping SSE only while the process is alive and letting AlertStreamState sit at DISCONNECTED because that 'correctly arms the on-device floor via the existing degraded predicate'. The data-layer analysis says the same redefinition INVERTS the primary dedup layer and leaves the floor 'permanently armed' in background, and leans on the ack-gated episode guard instead. One PRD verdict is required; they cannot both be implemented.

WRIST ALERT TRANSPORT -- THREE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE RECOMMENDATIONS. Alerting recommends dropping the watch-local alert entirely and letting iPhone system mirroring be the only wrist buzz. Data layer recommends the same (iPhone local notification, watchOS mirrors it), calling it a simplification. Wear recommends the OPPOSITE -- schedule the notification ON THE WATCH via transferUserInfo -- explicitly because mirroring only occurs when the iPhone is locked. Wear is correct on the facts. So alerting's and data-layer's recommendations silently accept a wrist that stays SILENT whenever the iPhone is unlocked and in use, which is a parity regression: the Wear service vibrates unconditionally today. Wear's design is also strictly better because a locally-scheduled re-buzz ladder keeps alarming even if the phone dies.

FEATURE DELETIONS PRESENTED AS IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL, UNDER A STRICT-PARITY MANDATE. (a) Wear recommends deleting cfg_theme and cfg_show_seconds from the wire contract; settings recommends keeping a trimmed toggle set that drops 'Show Seconds'. (b) The AI/meal/settings analysis recommends dropping the draggable meal FAB, its per-device position persistence, and its VoiceOver 'Reset position to default' custom action. Both are probably right, but 'delete a shipped user-facing control' must be an explicit PRD decision, not an aside, when the mandate says 'every feature currently supported'.

ROUNDING: 'PORT EXACTLY' AND 'DELIBERATELY IMPROVE' ARE STATED AS THE SAME RECOMMENDATION. Core display picks dot-decimal plus half-up for EVERY displayed number, calls it 'a deliberate, documented improvement over Android rather than a defect port', and in the same breath requires tests pinning exact string equality with Android. These conflict for every locale-formatted value (IoB, basal, battery, reservoir, TIR%, CV%, GMI) on a comma-decimal device: Android emits '1,23u', the recommendation emits '1.23u'. It cannot both match Android strings and fix Android's mixed-separator inconsistency. The test contract must be scoped to en-US strings plus the pinned cross-surface glucose fixtures.

BOLUS-HISTORY 'BG' COLUMN: THE MANDATE CONTRADICTS ITSELF. Core display flags that the Recent-Boluses and Bolus-History BG column prints the raw mg/dL integer with no conversion and no unit label, and explicitly leaves 'replicate or fix' undecided. Strict parity says replicate; but replicating means an mmol/L user reads '65' as though it were their unit on a clinical surface, which is the exact failure class the drift guard and the CodeRabbit Medical-Safety gate exist to prevent. This is the one place where the parity mandate and the safety posture point in opposite directions.

SAME ENGINE, TWO SPECS: NIGHTSCOUT CURSOR PERSISTENCE. The plugin analysis requires persisting the cursor after every page (Android persists only at loop exit and on the stall guard) so a 30-second BGAppRefreshTask can converge across runs. The data-layer analysis describes the same engine as 'ports verbatim' without that change. Under the data-layer spec, a first-run backfill in a background window never converges and repeatedly expires, which iOS punishes with reduced future scheduling.

MAX_QUEUE_SIZE. The data-layer analysis requires raising it well above 5000 as a mandatory parameter change; every other analysis assumes byte-identical queue logic. A real, defensible divergence -- but it must be recorded as one.

SIMULATED DRIVER BUILD GATING. Plugin says 'gate behind the feature gate so it can be excluded from production builds while remaining available in TestFlight if desired'; core display says 'first-class Debug target dependency'; wear says 'ship it behind a debug build configuration'. If the simulated driver is reachable in an externally distributed TestFlight build, the app contains a fabricated-glucose source in a medical binary -- an App Review and patient-safety problem. Android already hard-gates its injectors to BuildConfig.DEBUG at two independent levels (store getter/setter and again in the ViewModel).

APP-GROUP / SETTINGS-TRANSPORT ASSUMPTIONS ARE NOT UNIFORM. Core display proposes App Group UserDefaults plus WidgetCenter reloads plus WatchConnectivity for the phone/Watch hop, and notes App Groups do not span devices. Wear independently states the same fact and calls it 'a common and expensive misconception', and requires TWO separate App Groups. The plugin analysis proposes putting driver settings in a per-driver UserDefaults suite, and the data-layer analysis proposes persisting floor cooldown state 'to the App Group'. Nobody owns a single settings-storage topology, and this is exactly the kind of thing that silently forks into two sources of truth for the glucose unit.

must_ask_pm.question: The project is licensed GPL-3.0-only, and the Medtronic driver is a direct GPL-3.0 runtime dependency (org.openminimed:javasake) plus line-for-line ports of OpenMinimed code whose copyright is held by third parties (palmarci, drfubar, Morten Fyhn Amundsen, Stenium, planiitis). Apple's Developer Program License Agreement -- which governs TestFlight identically to the App Store -- imposes usage and device restrictions that conflict with GPLv3 sections 6 and 10; this is the VLC precedent and the FSF's stated position. How do we clear this before any code is written: (a) the copyright holders add a GPLv3 section 7 additional permission explicitly allowing Apple-platform distribution -- which requires the OpenMinimed authors' consent for the Medtronic driver, not just the project lead's; (b) relicense the project and ship Medtronic support only if OpenMinimed relicenses too; (c) ship iOS as Tandem-only under a relicensed codebase, dropping Medtronic; or (d) abandon TestFlight for a self-build/sideload distribution model, which forecloses the stated plan?
must_ask_pm.why_it_cannot_be_inferred: No subsystem analysis raised this at all. It is a legal and governance question that requires consent from named third-party copyright holders outside this repo. It blocks the stated distribution channel entirely, so it must be resolved before the port is scoped, not after. The repo can tell us the license and the provenance (docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md is explicit that the Medtronic driver is 'a direct dependency / port' used 'with the explicit permission of the OpenMinimed author... who relicensed the work to GPL-3.0 for this purpose'), but it cannot tell us whether those parties will grant an Apple-platform exception.
options: GPLv3 §7 additional permission from all holders, including OpenMinimed
Relicense the project; ship Medtronic only if OpenMinimed relicenses
iOS ships Tandem-only; Medtronic reachable only via Nightscout/backend
Abandon TestFlight for self-build distribution (forecloses the stated plan)

must_ask_pm.question: Server-generated alerts cannot reach a suspended or terminated iOS app by any means other than APNs, and an APNs auth key is issued to the app's Apple Developer Team and scoped to its bundle ID -- so a self-hoster cannot mint one. Which trust posture do we take: (a) no push at all, so backend alerts arrive only while the app is running and the on-device floor covers everything else (self-hosting stays pure; iOS backend alerting is materially weaker than Android's, which holds an SSE foreground service open indefinitely); (b) the project operates a push relay that self-hosted backends post through, meaning alert metadata transits infrastructure the user does not control; or (c) the project distributes its APNs signing key to self-hosters, letting any key holder push arbitrary notifications to every install?
must_ask_pm.why_it_cannot_be_inferred: Raised independently by three subsystems (alerting, plugin/Nightscout, data layer) with the same three-or-four-way fork and no way to choose between them. It is a privacy, trust, and infrastructure-ownership decision, not a technical one. The contract already reserves the wire slot (DeviceRegistrationRequest.platform includes 'ios' in contract/openapi.json, and device_token is today only a locally generated UUID), so the wire is not the blocker -- the posture is.
options: No push; SSE-while-alive plus the on-device floor, documented as a known iOS regression
Project-operated push relay (project holds the key and sees alert metadata)
Distribute the APNs key to self-hosters (anyone holding it can push to every install)

must_ask_pm.question: Bypassing Do Not Disturb, Focus, and the silent switch for urgent lows requires the com.apple.developer.usernotifications.critical-alerts entitlement, which Apple grants only after manually reviewing a written request tied to a specific developer account, and can decline. Two decisions: (1) under what legal entity do we apply -- this is an open-source project with an individual copyright holder and no company, which materially affects the odds; and (2) if it is declined, do we ship on the freely available Time Sensitive level (which breaks through Focus but not the silent switch or a muted volume, and cannot even detect that the phone is muted), or do we treat the entitlement as a launch blocker for the alerting feature?
must_ask_pm.why_it_cannot_be_inferred: Android gets DND bypass from a normal install-time permission (ACCESS_NOTIFICATION_POLICY, verified in the manifest) and raises alarm-stream volume with MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS. Neither has any self-serve iOS equivalent. Three subsystems rate this critical; the wear analysis explicitly names the legal-entity question as one 'this repo cannot answer'. The ship-if-denied call is a risk-appetite judgment about whether an alarm the phone can silence is an acceptable product for overnight lows.
options: Apply as an individual; ship the Time Sensitive fallback with explicit honest copy if denied
Apply under a newly formed entity to improve the odds; accept the delay
Treat the grant as a hard launch blocker for the alerting feature

must_ask_pm.question: The Android app supports plaintext HTTP to a self-hosted LAN backend behind an acknowledged opt-in (network_security_config permits cleartext globally; UrlSecurityPolicy is the sole in-app guard, since neither platform's config can express CIDR ranges). On iOS this needs an ATS exception in Info.plist that is visible to Beta App Review on every version's first external build, on an app that already carries four background modes, Bluetooth, a reverse-engineered pump protocol, and AI-generated carb estimates. Do we (a) ship the ATS exception and carry a standing review risk to preserve plain-HTTP LAN self-hosting, or (b) require HTTPS on iOS and drop the insecure-LAN opt-in, directing self-hosters to a reverse proxy, a user-installed private CA (which iOS trusts by default, unlike Android 7+), or a mesh VPN -- a deliberate removal of a shipped capability?
must_ask_pm.why_it_cannot_be_inferred: Three subsystems reached three different technical recommendations (NSAllowsArbitraryLoads / NSAllowsLocalNetworking / https-only) and disagree factually about whether NSAllowsLocalNetworking covers RFC1918 -- that part is settleable by testing. What is not settleable is the risk appetite: option (a) keeps parity but attaches review exposure to a safety-critical app whose distribution is already in question, and option (b) removes a feature the Android app ships behind a deliberate consent dialog.
options: Ship the ATS exception; keep UrlSecurityPolicy as the sole in-app guard (Android's architecture)
HTTPS-only on iOS; drop the LAN-HTTP opt-in and document private-CA HTTPS as the supported path

must_ask_pm.question: Medtronic MiniMed pairing requires the phone to act as a BLE peripheral advertising a human-readable local name that the user selects from the pump's own menu. iOS ignores CBAdvertisementDataLocalNameKey while backgrounded and relegates advertised service UUIDs to an overflow area readable only by iOS devices scanning for them explicitly, and gives less control over advertised identity than Android even in the foreground. If a foreground-attended CBPeripheralManager prototype fails against real MiniMed hardware, what is the posture: (a) ship iOS as Tandem-only and tell Medtronic users iOS is not supported; (b) ship Medtronic as cloud-mediated only (Nightscout or backend), surfaced as a different, clearly labelled capability rather than a degraded pairing; or (c) hold the iOS launch until a direct path is found?
must_ask_pm.why_it_cannot_be_inferred: The plugin analysis correctly identifies this as the highest-variance unknown in the subsystem and says to prototype it first, but the contingency is a product-scope decision about which users the iOS app serves at launch. It cannot be inferred from the parity mandate, because the mandate is unmeetable for that device if the prototype fails. Note that tools/medtronic-ble-spike/ already contains an offline SAKE harness and an android-peripheral-probe support matrix, so the prototype can be scoped precisely -- but the answer to 'and if it fails?' still has to come from the product owner.
options: Medtronic supported cloud-mediated only, labelled as a distinct capability
Hold the iOS launch until direct Medtronic pairing is proven

safe_assumptions: Q (core display): 'When the iPhone is unreachable or suspended, what must the Apple Watch still show?' ANSWER: parity settles it. The Android watch is a pure relay fed by a phone foreground service and has no independent data path. Option (a) -- a degraded watch showing an explicit 'no recent data from phone' state -- IS parity, and is exactly what the ported WristCoverage decay (receivedAt + advertised timeout, clamped 10 s..30 min, fail-closed on unknown/aged/future-skewed) already produces. Independent watch-to-backend fetch and watch-to-pump Core Bluetooth are additive scope; defer both. One narrow exception is already justified independently: the watch calling the backend directly for AI chat, because it deletes the WearChatRelayService foreground-service hack and the documented 30s-vs-90s timeout mismatch.

Q (alerting): 'Does the coverage claim say "watching" or "watching, but you may not hear it"?' ANSWER: the repo's own honesty architecture settles it. AlertFloorStatus mirrors the FIRING gates; audibility is not a firing gate. Keep the always-visible claim binary and gate-derived. Surface soundSetting / criticalAlertSetting / scheduledDeliverySetting / timeSensitiveSetting as distinct FloorNotWatchingReason-style entries in the Notifications settings card ONLY when they would actually suppress -- which is the pattern Android already ships (the card renders 'Disabled -- alerts will not appear on your phone' in ERROR color). State the irreducible blind spot (the ring/silent switch and volume are unreadable by any public API) once in onboarding and once in Settings, not on every glance.

Every 'impossible' verdict is unanimous and correct under Apple's published rules; parity cannot apply to a capability the platform forbids, and no PM input is needed to accept the documented substitutes: runtime/custom plugin loading and the Custom Plugins install UI (Guideline 2.5.2 plus code-signing enforcement); in-app APK self-update; wear APK push and WatchFaceInstaller; third-party custom watch faces and the watch-face gallery; BootCompletedReceiver / launch-on-boot; foreground services; a persistent non-dismissible ongoing notification; setBypassDnd by application decision; system alarm-volume boost and restore; custom per-alert vibration waveforms; the RingtoneManager arbitrary-URI sound picker; notification channels as a user-tunable OS surface; and holding an SSE stream open while suspended.

cfg_theme and cfg_show_seconds: DELETE. Verified as dead code on Android -- validated, stored, and read by nothing. Deleting a control with no behavior behind it is not a parity break. Record it in the PRD as a verified no-op so it is not later mistaken for a regression. Rebinding 'theme' to the watch app's own screens (which are full colour and under our control) is a strict improvement.

Draggable meal FAB: DROP the drag, the per-device saved position, and the VoiceOver 'Reset position' action. The drag exists to compensate for an Android-specific occlusion problem. A fixed bottom-trailing button above the tab bar safe area, plus a redundant 'Log a meal' row at the top of Home, plus a preserved bottom content inset, delivers the same user outcome (button never obscures content; reachable) using layout instead of user labor. Keep every gate exactly: absent with no backend, absent when meal intelligence is locally off, visible on a transient probe failure, re-checked on both success and failure paths.

Bolus-history 'BG' column printing raw mg/dL with no unit label: FIX IT, and log it as a deliberate, documented divergence. Parity means feature parity, not defect parity. Every other glucose surface in the app converts; the repo's own CodeRabbit Medical-Safety path rule requires that any value compared or displayed as glucose respect the canonical-mg/dL-plus-18.0156 discipline; and shipping an unlabelled mg/dL integer to an mmol/L user on a clinical surface is precisely the desync class the cross-repo drift guard exists to prevent.

Rounding and locale: use Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX") with explicit half-up rounding for every number the dashboard renders, and pin the exact-tie cases (12.5%, 100.5, 0.125). GlucoseFormat already forces Locale.US on Android specifically because cross-surface string equality is load-bearing and the release log scrubber's regex depends on a dot separator. Scope the equality tests to en-US Android strings plus the pinned cross-surface fixtures (54→3.0, 70→3.9, 99→5.5, 100→5.6, 120→6.7, 180→10.0, 250→13.9, 400→22.2, 20→1.1, 500→27.8); do not attempt to reproduce Android's comma-decimal behavior for IoB/TIR/CV/GMI, which is a defect.

Simulated pump/CGM driver: build it as a first-class day-one deliverable, and EXCLUDE it from every externally distributed configuration including TestFlight. Android already hard-gates its injectors to BuildConfig.DEBUG at two independent levels precisely because injections write to the same cache that drives the real glucose hero and can fire a real OS alarm. A fabricated-glucose source reachable in a distributed medical binary is an App Review and patient-safety problem, not a convenience tradeoff.

AI chat in-flight request cancelled on backgrounding: accept the narrower contract and say so honestly on return. The Android transcript is deliberately in-memory only, so a background-URLSession-delivered answer would have nowhere to land without introducing a durable store of health-related conversation content the Android app deliberately does not have. Reserve background URLSession for the watch-relay fallback path.

Whether to build widgets and complications at all: yes, and frame them correctly. Android ships no widgets, tiles, shortcuts, or deep links -- verified. iOS widgets and complications are the SUBSTITUTES for the two things iOS removes (the Wear custom watch face, and the foreground-service notification that is the only always-visible honest-coverage surface). They are how parity is approximated, not new product scope. The pre-baked-timeline-entry technique (entries scheduled at timestamp + staleAfterMs and + tooStaleAfterMs, and at the coverage validUntil) is not an optimization -- it is the only way the freshness and coverage decay survives without a running process, and it costs zero refresh budget.

Localization: no i18n obligation. The repo has a single values/ resource set with no values-xx and a 9-line strings.xml; essentially all copy is inline Kotlin. Inline Swift strings are acceptable parity.

HealthKit, data export, deep links, and backup: no obligation. None exist on Android; the manifest sets allowBackup=false and MainActivity is exported but processes no intent data (with an explicit comment requiring re-evaluation if deep links are ever added). Do not add HealthKit write -- it would create a new therapeutic-adjacent data path with no Android counterpart.

Storage protection classes: Apple's rules settle it, no product input needed. Keychain items (auth tokens, pump pairing secrets, JPAKE derived secret and server nonce) use kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly -- AfterFirstUnlock so background BLE reconnect works on a locked device, ThisDeviceOnly so pump pairing secrets never leave via iCloud Keychain or an encrypted backup. Databases use FileProtectionType.completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication, never .complete. Add the first-run purge keyed on a UserDefaults flag, because iOS Keychain items survive app deletion while UserDefaults does not -- this also fixes the Android bug where removing a plugin left plugin_creds_<id> behind.

Notification authorization options: request [.alert, .sound, .badge, .criticalAlert] in ONE call at the end of BOTH onboarding completion paths (after login and after 'Use without a server'), mirroring exactly where Android requests POST_NOTIFICATIONS on both paths. iOS presents the prompt once per install, so a later request for .criticalAlert silently no-ops. Never use .provisional -- provisional delivery is quiet, which would silently disable every alarm. Requesting .criticalAlert before the entitlement is granted is harmless.

SSE while the process is alive, plus opportunistic pulls of /api/v1/alerts/pending, plus the on-device floor: Apple's rules settle it. Background URLSessionConfiguration supports only file-backed upload and download tasks; URLSessionDataTask and streaming responses are explicitly unsupported, and a suspended app has no runloop. Keep every hard-won piece of AlertStreamService that is transport-agnostic: the connection-generation guard, the single-flight reconnect CAS, min(1000 * 2^min(attempt,6), 60_000) backoff, the 401/403 jump to max(5, attempt), STABLE_CONNECTION_MS = 10_000, the idempotent start, the 75 s read timeout (2.5 heartbeats), and reconcile-pending-acks on stream open.

TestFlight posture: start with the internal group (up to 100 testers, no Beta App Review) for the developer's own loop and batch external releases so Beta App Review lands on a predictable cadence. Automate build-and-upload in CI so the 90-day build expiry is a non-event, and surface the installed build's expiry in-app with a countdown inside 14 days -- for a user relying on overnight low alerts, an expired build is a silent monitoring outage. All of this follows from Apple's published rules plus the stated one-developer workflow.

Keep the _ts / monotonic seq dedup-buster on the phone-to-watch payload. updateApplicationContext is documented to replace the stored context but is not documented to redeliver an identical one, and the heartbeat's deliverability is load-bearing for the dead-phone detector. A monotonic sequence number costs nothing.

Throwing initializers, not precondition: settled by the language and the Android design intent together. Kotlin's require/check throw catchable exceptions and the platform relies on catching them (SettingsViewModel wraps metadata and settingsDescriptor() in try/catch(Throwable) specifically so a misbehaving plugin degrades instead of crashing). Swift's precondition traps the process and is untestable. Use throwing inits for every value originating from a device, driver, or backend; reserve precondition for genuine programmer errors (double-initializing the registry is the only one). Never clamp as an escape from the trap -- that converts a loud driver bug into a wrong number on a glucose chart.
top_port_risks: GPL-3.0-only versus Apple's Developer Program License Agreement blocks the entire stated distribution channel, before a line of Swift is written. TestFlight is governed by the same DPLA as the App Store; GPLv3 §6 (Installation Information / anti-Tivoization) and §10 (no further restrictions) conflict with Apple's device and usage restrictions -- the VLC precedent and the FSF's stated position. Worse, the Medtronic driver is a direct GPL-3.0 runtime dependency (org.openminimed:javasake 0.2.0) plus line-for-line GPL-3.0 ports whose copyright is held by third parties, so the project lead cannot unilaterally relicense it or add a §7 App Store exception. No subsystem analysis raised this. It must be resolved first because it can change what gets built.

Roughly 10,400 LOC of unanalyzed, safety-critical BLE protocol and crypto with no Apple-platform library to stand on. Tandem EC-JPAKE needs raw P-256 point arithmetic that CryptoKit does not expose (swift-crypto/_CryptoExtras/BoringSSL or hand-rolled BigInt); Medtronic needs a Swift reimplementation of the JVM-only JavaSake 6-stage SAKE handshake and SeqCrypt cipher, plus AES-CMAC, which build.gradle.kts notes the JCE lacks and CryptoKit also lacks. Add CRC16, packetization and reassembly, and 973 lines of byte-level opcode parsing with non-uniform milliunit scaling, epoch offsets and firmware-dependent layouts. This is the longest pole in the project and it is the layer where a defect becomes a wrong glucose or a wrong insulin number. Mitigate by porting tools/medtronic-ble-spike's captured-trace acceptance harness to Swift FIRST -- it makes the crypto verifiable with no pump, which matters enormously given the Simulator has no Core Bluetooth.

iOS provides no background execution guarantee, so the on-device alert floor and the coverage claim become conditional on Core Bluetooth producing wake events. Android's foreground service polls every 15 s forever, which is also the ~30 s BLE keep-alive. Compounding: force-quitting from the app switcher permanently disables ALL background relaunch including CB state restoration and silent push until the user manually reopens; nothing runs after a reboot until first unlock; Low Power Mode removes the backfill path. All three are invisible to the app while they happen and are the most common way an iOS diabetes app goes silent. Mitigation is honesty, not engineering: a dead-man's-switch local notification rescheduled on every wake, a Lock Screen widget whose timeline carries a pre-computed future entry that flips to NOT-watching at the exact expiry, and persisting a last-ran timestamp so the gap is reported on next launch.

The Critical Alerts entitlement is Apple-granted on manual review and may be declined. Without it an urgent low cannot bypass the silent switch, Do Not Disturb, or a muted volume -- and the app cannot even detect that the phone is muted, because neither the ring/silent switch position nor the ringer volume is readable by any public API. Android gets all of this from install-time permissions (ACCESS_NOTIFICATION_POLICY, MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS, verified in the manifest). A denial does not merely degrade a feature; it invalidates the honest-coverage claim the whole alerting architecture is built to protect. Apply on day one and treat it as a schedule dependency.

Core Bluetooth does not exist in the iOS Simulator (CBCentralManager reports .unsupported), and the developer's primary loop is Simulator-based. Every capability downstream of the pump link -- connection state, the poll sequence, freshness tiers, pump-sourced chart and card data, the alert relay state machine, coverage claims, history overlays, both pairing flows -- is unreachable without a first-class simulated driver. That driver must be built BEFORE the dashboard, with recorded fixture histories spanning 3H/24H/7D/30D, all eight trend values, out-of-range and clock-skewed readings, warmup and signal-loss (same sensor timestamp returned repeatedly), and scripted connection-state transitions.

The Simulator produces false positives on precisely the properties that matter most here, each of which fails only on hardware and often only after hours. It does not validate entitlements (a locally added critical-alerts entitlement APPEARS to work); does not enforce Local Network Privacy (a LAN backend works perfectly then fails opaquely on device); does not enforce Data Protection or Keychain lock-state semantics (the device is effectively always unlocked, so AfterFirstUnlock-vs-WhenUnlocked is indistinguishable); does not enforce WidgetKit or WatchConnectivity budgets or BGTaskScheduler cadence; has no Focus, Do Not Disturb, or ring/silent switch; has no haptics on watchOS; has no camera; and does not faithfully simulate suspension or termination, so a while-true polling loop appears to work. A mandatory on-device smoke checklist gated before every upload is not optional process -- it is the only validation for a life-safety path.

Medtronic advertise-and-wait pairing may be unachievable on iOS. The flow requires the pump to discover the phone by a human-readable advertised name, but iOS ignores CBAdvertisementDataLocalNameKey while backgrounded and relegates advertised service UUIDs to an overflow area readable only by iOS devices scanning for them explicitly. Foreground advertising gives less control over advertised identity than Android. If MiniMed firmware will not accept an iOS peripheral's advertisement, parity is unmeetable for that device. Prototype CBPeripheralManager against real hardware as the first iOS driver task, ahead of any UI work.

The 20..500 mg/dL bound has NO OWNER and lives in roughly fourteen enumerated code sites plus the wear mirror, held equal only by build-time drift guards that have no iOS counterpart yet. iOS multiplies the surfaces: app, watch app, iOS widget extension, watch widget extension, two separate App Groups, and no shared defaults across the phone/Watch boundary. The 18.0156 factor and the never-mentioned TANDEM_EPOCH_OFFSET = 1199145600 are in the same regime, and the epoch offset is worse -- getting it wrong shifts every timestamp by decades and silently destroys the freshness architecture everything else rests on. docs/adr/0003 already records the consolidation follow-up; the port is the moment to do it.

Mistranslating Kotlin require/check. A literal transcription to precondition traps the process -- a crash loop in a monitoring app, possibly during a background Bluetooth wake the user never sees. The inverse mistake, clamping to avoid the trap, silently fabricates a plausible glucose or dose on a chart the patient reads. Both failure modes are strictly worse than Android's. The Android unit-test suite that pins drop-not-clamp behavior (NightscoutDataMapperTest, SafetyLimitsTest, the extract* driver tests) is the enforcement mechanism, since the interfaces never enforced it on Android either -- carry it over as the acceptance suite.

Wrist alert delivery has three contradictory designs across analyses, and two of them accept a silent wrist whenever the iPhone is unlocked and in use, because iOS mirrors notifications to the Watch only when the phone is locked. That is a parity regression: the Wear service vibrates unconditionally today. The correct design (schedule the notification ON the watch from a transferUserInfo wake) is also strictly better than Android, because a locally scheduled re-buzz ladder keeps alarming an ongoing emergency even if the phone dies -- but the ladder must terminate once the underlying reading ages past TOO_STALE, with a final notification saying the data is stale and nothing is watching.

App Review exposure is compounded rather than additive: Guideline 1.4.1 medical scrutiny; a reverse-engineered pump protocol with firmware-derived SAKE key material; third-party manufacturer trademarks (Tandem, Medtronic, Nightscout); AI-generated carb estimates adjacent to insulin dosing; an ATS cleartext exception; four background modes; Bluetooth central AND peripheral roles; and Beta App Review on every version's first external build. Lead with the strongest true fact -- read-only monitoring, no therapeutic write anywhere in the SDK surface -- and resolve the CalibrationTarget contradiction before submission so that claim is literally true of the shipped binary.

watchOS complications render in an accented/tinted mode that flattens hue. The alerts bell encodes its entire six-branch coverage-honesty decision in grey/amber/red, and the glucose graph encodes basal, bolus, activity-mode bands and per-segment glucose banding entirely in colour. A literal port makes 'everything is fine' and 'your phone is dead and nothing is watching' pixel-identical -- deleting the dead-phone cue in exactly the case it exists for. Re-encode on SF Symbol, shape and text before writing any complication view, and gate the merge on greyscale screenshots of all six branches being distinguishable.

WidgetKit and WatchConnectivity budgets are metered and small relative to the data cadence: roughly 40-70 timeline reloads per day for a placed iOS widget, and historically ~50 high-priority complication transfers per day, against 288 CGM readings and an Android coverage heartbeat that fires every 3 minutes (~480 transfers/day). A push-per-reading design will appear to work in development and silently stop updating partway through the day on real hardware. Pre-baked timeline entries must be the primary mechanism, metered transfers reserved for material change, and remainingComplicationUserInfoTransfers surfaced in the Settings telemetry card.

Numeric divergence between Java's HALF_UP formatter and C/Foundation's round-half-to-even: a TIR bucket of exactly 12.5% renders 13% on Android and 12% in a naive Swift port; a mean glucose of exactly 100.5 renders 101 vs 100. Reachable with small reading counts, and the mmol glucose fixture passes only by luck (no tie is reachable in 20..500 for the 18.0156 divisor). Route every displayed number through one helper with en_US_POSIX and explicit half-up rounding -- note NumberFormatter defaults to .halfEven.

Swift Codable does not apply a property's default when a JSON key is absent, whereas Moshi's Kotlin adapter does. Fields such as is_automated, acknowledged, raw_accepted, raw_duplicates and source would turn a tolerated omission on Android into a hard parse failure on iOS, potentially failing an entire alert page -- which the sync engine would then classify as transient and retry forever against a condition that will never change. Decode every defaulted field with decodeIfPresent, and extend the contract smoke test with an assertion that cannot fail on Android and therefore does not exist there. The same class of defect applies to ISO-8601 fractional seconds, which Python emits only when non-zero.

CBPeripheral identifiers are per-app UUIDs, not MAC addresses, and are not stable across app reinstall -- while iOS Keychain items DO survive app deletion. A reinstalled app can therefore hold live pump pairing secrets (including the JPAKE derived secret and server nonce) keyed to a device identifier that no longer resolves, presenting as 'unpaired' while the OS-level bond is intact. Model stored identity as UUID plus, where the protocol exposes one, the pump serial read after connect; retrieve by identifier then by connected-peripherals-with-services before falling back to a scan; and purge driver credentials on first run after a fresh install, keyed off a UserDefaults flag.
